paragraphs.en: The material abundance of this era, Dunlop writes, spawned "a complex gastronomic culture in which food was not only cooked and enjoyed, but also elaborated, discussed and documented".
paragraphs.zh: 邓洛普写道，这个时代的物质丰富催生了一种复杂的美食文化，在这种文化中，食物不仅被烹饪和享用，还被精心制作、讨论和记录。

paragraphs.en: Records of the Fresh and Strange, written by a 10th-century scholar and poet, celebrated specialities of the lower Yangtze delta such as sweet pears, loquats and a "noodle so pliable that it could be tied in knots", as Jin Feng writes in Tasting Paradise on Earth, a history of the region's food.
paragraphs.zh: 《清异录》由一位10世纪的学者兼诗人所著，书中盛赞了长江三角洲下游的特产，如甜梨、枇杷和一种"柔韧可打结的面条"。正如金雯在描写该地区饮食史的著作《人间滋味》中所写。

paragraphs.en: Su Dongpo, an imperial official and one of China's most revered poets, wrote about humble dishes of pork and cabbage.
paragraphs.zh: 苏轼是一位朝廷官员，也是中国最受尊敬的诗人之一，他曾描写过猪肉白菜这类家常菜肴。

paragraphs.en: (His recipe for turnip soup, which was recorded in 1098, survives to this day.)
paragraphs.zh: (他1098年记录的萝卜汤配方一直流传至今。)

paragraphs.en: Appreciation of fine food was a mark of culture, like being accomplished in calligraphy, painting and poetry.
paragraphs.zh: 品味美食是文化修养的标志，如同精通书法、绘画与诗歌一般。

paragraphs.en: In 1127, the Song capital city of Kaifeng fell to invaders from Manchuria, forcing the remnants of the imperial court to flee south.
paragraphs.zh: 1127年，宋朝都城开封被来自满洲的侵略者攻陷，迫使朝廷残余势力南逃。

paragraphs.en: On the shores of West Lake they built a new capital, Hangzhou, which became the largest and richest city in the world at that time.
paragraphs.zh: 他们在西湖畔建起了一座新都城——杭州，当时它成了世界上最大最富庶的城市。

paragraphs.en: On a visit during the late 13th century, Marco Polo was impressed by the numbers of those "accustomed to dainty living, to the point of eating fish and meat at one meal".
paragraphs.zh: 13世纪末的一次访问中，马可·波罗对当地“习惯于精致生活，甚至一餐同时享用鱼肉和兽肉”的人数之多感到惊讶。

paragraphs.en: With its mix of natives and refugees from the north, the city was something of a melting pot, which was reflected in its cooking.
paragraphs.zh: 这座城市融合了本地人和北方难民，堪称一个大熔炉，这种特点也体现在其烹饪风格中。

paragraphs.en: Northern dishes were remade with southern ingredients: shrimp was substituted for mutton, and pastries became lighter and flakier.
paragraphs.zh: 北方菜肴用南方食材重新制作：虾替代了羊肉，糕点变得更轻盈酥脆。

paragraphs.en: The fusion of regional cooking styles – the art of mixture, on a large scale – created a truly national cuisine, although not everyone was pleased.
paragraphs.zh: 区域烹饪风格的融合——大规模混合的艺术——创造出了真正意义上的全国性美食，尽管并非所有人都对此感到满意。

paragraphs.en: "Food and drink have become all confused, with no longer any distinction between southern and northern," one scholar complained.
paragraphs.zh: 一位学者抱怨道：“饮食之道已全然混淆，南北风味再无分别。”

paragraphs.en: In The Eastern Capital: A Dream of Splendour, the twelfth-century gourmet Meng Yuanlao described, street by street and dish by dish, the culinary delights of Kaifeng around 1120, when he lived there as a young man: "Even if there are only two men sitting across from each other, they must use a set of bowls with fluted handles … Even if one drinks alone, such items as silver bowls are used.
paragraphs.zh: 在《东京梦华录》中，十二世纪的美食家孟元老以街道为序、以菜肴为目，逐笔描绘了约1120年他青年时代所居汴京的饮食盛景："凡两人对坐饮酒，必用注碗一副……虽独酌亦用银盂之类"。

paragraphs.en: The fruits and vegetables are fine and exquisite."
paragraphs.zh: 这些水果和蔬菜精致而细腻。

paragraphs.en: He recalled his favourite dishes: quail eggs, fried loyang snow pears.
paragraphs.zh: 他回忆起自己最爱的菜肴：鹌鹑蛋、炸洛阳雪梨。

paragraphs.en: By the time Meng wrote this, the city as he had known it no longer existed; it had fallen to invaders two decades before.
paragraphs.zh: 等到孟写这段文字的时候，他记忆中的那座城市早已不复存在；二十年前，它就已沦陷于侵略者之手。

paragraphs.en: Food is ephemeral, but so are places: buildings, streets, even a flourishing capital can disappear like a fondly remembered meal.
paragraphs.zh: 食物易逝，地方亦然：建筑、街道，甚至一座繁华的都城都可能像记忆中那顿美餐般消逝无踪。

paragraphs.en: At the root of the Chinese gastronomic tradition is a yearning for a lost age.
paragraphs.zh: 中国美食传统的根源是对逝去时代的深切怀念。

paragraphs.en: Through words, we create what no longer exists in the world.
paragraphs.zh: 通过文字，我们创造世上已不复存在之物。

paragraphs.en: Dunlop has engaged deeply with this tradition.
paragraphs.zh: 邓洛普深入参与了这一传统。

paragraphs.en: She can pinpoint the earliest appearance in the gastronomical literature of soy sauce, the first use of the word for "stir-fry" and the etymological origins of the term dim sum.
paragraphs.zh: 她能准确指出酱油在美食文献中的最早记载、"炒"字的首度使用以及"点心"一词的词源来历。

paragraphs.en: Like so many of her Chinese predecessors, she regards food with a moralist's eye.
paragraphs.zh: 和许多中国先辈一样，她以道德家的眼光看待食物。

paragraphs.en: She would like readers not just to appreciate the wonders of Chinese cooking but also to value the healthy and sustainable approach that lies behind it.
paragraphs.zh: 她希望读者不仅能欣赏中国烹饪的奇妙之处，还能重视其背后蕴含的健康与可持续理念。

paragraphs.en: In other ways, she blows up the tradition altogether.
paragraphs.zh: 在其他方面 她彻底颠覆了传统。

paragraphs.en: Dunlop, as a woman who cooks and writes, breaks with a long line of male intellectuals who tended to discourse about food from a certain remove and didn't actually cook.
paragraphs.zh: 作为一位既下厨又写作的女性，邓洛普打破了长期以来男性知识分子倾向于保持一定距离谈论美食却从不真正动手烹饪的传统。

paragraphs.en: The sage Mencius said: "The gentleman keeps his distance from the kitchen.")
paragraphs.zh: (圣贤孟子有言："君子远庖厨。")

paragraphs.en: Knowing how to eat well was a sign of refinement, but cooking itself has always been low-status.
paragraphs.zh: 懂得如何吃得好曾是高雅的标志，但烹饪本身始终被视为低等行当。

paragraphs.en: Dunlop's classmates in culinary school were almost all young men from working-class or rural families.
paragraphs.zh: 邓洛普在烹饪学校的同学几乎都是来自工薪阶层或农村家庭的年轻男子。

paragraphs.en: "If we were making pork balls, we had to pound the meat to a paste with the backs of our cleavers," she writes.
paragraphs.zh: "如果我们做猪肉丸子，就得用菜刀背把肉剁成肉泥，"她写道。

paragraphs.en: "If we were using walnuts, we had to crack them open, soak them and then, laboriously, peel off their skins."
paragraphs.zh: 如果我们用的是核桃，就得先敲开它们，浸泡一下，然后费劲地剥掉外皮。

paragraphs.en: Cooking is labour, and Dunlop can convey the painstaking multiday process of preparing a dish like braised pomelo pith with shrimp eggs while also tracing the Chinese predilection for using such unlikely ingredients back to the 16th century BC.
paragraphs.zh: 烹饪是项体力活，邓洛普既能描述用虾籽煨柚子瓤这类需耗时数日的繁琐工序，也能将中国人偏好此类冷门食材的渊源追溯至公元前16世纪。
